issues.detail: The Greek text includes 'ατενισας εις αυτον' (looked at him/himself), but the Vietnamese translation 'nhìn chăm vào người' is ambiguous. In context (Acts 9:18), 'αυτον' refers to the man (Ananias) who was speaking, but the Vietnamese 'người' can be interpreted as a general third person or the subject in some contexts. However, the primary issue is that 'ατενισας' implies a specific action of looking/gazing that is slightly weakened by the phrasing, but more importantly, the Greek structure 'σαυλος δε ο και παυλος' indicates 'Saul who is also called Paul'. The Vietnamese 'Sau-lơ cũng gọi là Phao-lô' captures the meaning well, but the omission of the specific object of the gaze or a slight shift in focus regarding the action of 'looking' can be flagged if it loses the directness of the Greek.
